notes: Repairs a production Auth0/Google callback-to-product session loop under FR-01 without changing provider or authorization policy.
Keeps small-token single-cookie compatibility while adding bounded HttpOnly cookie chunking so browser session transport does not depend on one large Set-Cookie payload.
Adds a post-callback session checkpoint that requires the browser-presented bearer token to be accepted by the existing Kairo session API before entering the product shell.
Authentication completion failures terminate at the existing sign-in recovery page instead of automatically restarting the OIDC flow.
No token length, bearer token, client secret or provider response body is logged as part of diagnosis or repair.

approvals.rationale: Owner said 'Go' after the live iOS Safari Auth0/Google callback redirect loop was diagnosed and a bounded FR-01 repair was proposed. Scope is limited to browser session handoff, fail-closed loop prevention, cleanup and regression coverage.
DEC-001, VS-16 and VS-25 remain unchanged: managed OIDC/Auth0 is still the identity provider boundary, API JWT validation remains strict and Workspace/Brand authorization stays Kairo-owned.

The same explicit 'Go' authorizes bounded branch implementation, deterministic regression tests and PR/CI publication for the diagnosed auth-session repair. It does not authorize certification, merge, release, production enablement or deployment.

evidence: Production iOS Safari recording showed repeated / -> /auth/login -> /auth/callback -> / 307 loop on VS-71 production.
Vercel runtime logs confirmed repeated callback/login/root redirects during the reproduction window while the Kairo API received no session request.
Deterministic unit/regression coverage has been added on the implementation branch; Product Intake, Security and CI are still pending.

postRelease.expectedOutcome: Google/Auth0 sign-in establishes one usable Kairo session without redirect loops on iOS Safari and desktop browsers.
